data.answer: Nimbus Labs holds a current SOC 2 Type II attestation for the Nimbus Ledger Sync platform, which covers the audit period from 1 January 2026 to 30 June 2026. The final report was issued on 14 August 2026 by Harlow & Pike LLP.
Yes, TLS certificates are issued by a public certificate authority and renewed automatically 30 days before they expire.

Customer data is stored in India by default on AWS Mumbai, but disaster recovery copies are held in Singapore. Because the disaster recovery replica is in Singapore, customers who need all copies of their data kept in India should discuss this with Nimbus Labs before signing.
Yes, customer administrators can connect their own SAML 2.0 identity provider to Nimbus Ledger Sync.
Yes, account numbers and UPI identifiers are additionally encrypted at the field level before they are written to the database so they remain protected even in database exports.

After a contract ends, customer data stays available for export for 90 days. Once that window closes, the data is deleted from production systems within 30 days, and backups containing that data expire on their normal 35-day cycle so the last copy is gone no later than 35 days after production deletion.
In an incident, the on-call engineer may take emergency production access for up to 2 hours without prior approval, and the Engineering Manager must approve it retrospectively within 24 hours.
Yes, Nimbus Labs reports to CERT-In within 6 hours of becoming aware of a reportable cyber incident, as required by Indian rules.
An external penetration test is performed once a year by CertiNova. The most recent test took place in March 2026.
